title: Gridfall Pizza — 142 Third Street, Gridfall
description: A takeout pizza shop on Third Street in Gridfall, run by three of the same family, on a storefront template that only knows how to sell products and a third-party order button that does not work on some phones.

products.name: Cheese Pizza, 16 inch
products.blurb:
Sixteen inches, eight cut, whole milk mozzarella we shred here.

The sauce is crushed tomatoes, salt and a little oregano, and it is not cooked before it goes on. If you like a sweet sauce you are not going to like ours, and we would rather you knew that now than found it out for sixteen dollars.

Dough is made the morning before and used the next day. We do about forty on a Tuesday and a hundred and twenty on a Friday, and on a Friday at 6:30 the wait is forty minutes no matter what the website tells you.
bullets: 16 inch, 8 cut. The 12 inch is [url=/p/p-small]a separate listing[/url] because the website will not do sizes
Toppings are $2.50 each on a 16 inch. The whole list is on [url=/p/p-toppings]the toppings page[/url]
Well done, light cheese, cut in squares, no cut at all — say so on the phone and it costs nothing
The left deck of the oven runs about fifteen degrees hot. If you want the one off the right deck, ask. Everyone who works here knows which is which

products.name: Pepperoni, 16 inch
products.blurb:
Cup pepperoni, the kind that curls and holds a little grease in it. Sixteen inches, eight cut.

Under the cheese, on top of the cheese, or both — both is $2.50 more and about a third of the orders on a Friday.

This is the single most ordered thing in the shop and has been every year since we started counting in 2011.

Looking for the best pizza in {{city_name}}? Gridfall Pizza has proudly served {{city_name}} and the surrounding {{region_name}} area since {{year_founded}}, offering handcrafted pies, fast delivery and unbeatable value for the whole family. Order online today!
bullets: Cup pepperoni. Not the flat kind. We tried the flat kind in 2013 for one order of it and went back
On top, underneath, or both. Both is $2.50
The paragraph at the bottom of the description is put there by the website company. We cannot delete it. We can only type above it
Half and half with any other pizza on the menu is fine and is the higher of the two prices

products.name: The Third Street, 16 inch
products.blurb:
Pepperoni, sausage, mushroom, onion and green pepper. Sixteen inches, eight cut, and it is heavy.

Nick Cortese put this on the menu in 1983 and called it the House. We kept the pizza and changed the name when we bought the shop, because it is the one thing on here that is only on here.

The sausage is bulk, browned in the morning, and it is the same sausage in the [url=/p/p-zititray]ziti tray[/url]. The mushrooms are canned. Nick used canned, we use canned, and the two times we have used fresh somebody has telephoned about it.

[b]The reviews on this page are the reviews of the whole shop.[/b] The order system puts the review link on the last item in the ticket, and the last item in the ticket is nearly always this, so this is where they all land. We cannot move them and we have stopped trying.
bullets: Pepperoni, sausage, mushroom, onion, green pepper. Any of the five off is fine and the price does not change
Takes about four minutes longer than a cheese because of the load. On a Friday assume fifty minutes
12 inch version is $17.50 at the counter. The website will not do sizes, so ring for it
Sausage is browned at 9:00 in the morning and we run out of it maybe twice a year, both times in October

reviews.title: Same as it was
reviews.body:
I have been getting this pizza since Nick had the shop and it is the same pizza. That is the entire review and it is meant as a compliment.

I ask for it off the right deck because the left one runs hot and they have never once made me feel like a nuisance about it.

reviews.title: Forty minutes late and cold
reviews.body:
Ordered 6:15, told 45 minutes, got it 7:40 and it was cold enough that the cheese had set.

The driver could not find the house and I will own half of that, because the number came off the post in the spring and I have not put it back.

The other half is that nobody rang me. My number is on the ticket. Two stars and I will order again in a month because there is nowhere else.

reviews.title: Sunday with my daughter's family
reviews.body:
Six of us at 5:30 on a Sunday and we were seated straight away at the window table without asking.

I had the pot roast, my wife had the haddock, the two little ones had the chicken fingers off the children's menu and ate about four between them. Rolls still come warm and they still bring more without being asked.

Separate checks for all six, no sighing, no confusion. The girl at the front is new and did fine.

Only complaint is the parking on this street after five, which is not their fault.

reviews.title: Excellent item, arrived as pictured
reviews.body: The item arrived promptly and was exactly as shown in the listing photograph. Packaging was secure and there was no damage in transit. Communication from the seller was prompt and professional throughout. I would not hesitate to purchase from this seller again and recommend them to anyone considering this product.

reviews.title: A Gridfall institution
reviews.body:
Gridfall Pizza has been a fixture of the Third Street business district since opening its doors in 2004, shortly after the closure of the Blue Kestrel Diner in 2004 left residents of the community without a gathering place.

The family-owned establishment survived the 2004 Gridfall substation fire and continues to serve local residents and visitors alike. Local officials have praised small businesses like this one for their contribution to the area economy.

Whether you are a longtime resident or just passing through Verity County, be sure to stop by and experience it for yourself.

reviews.title: $5 ANY LARGE ANY TOPPINGS
reviews.body: Why pay $24?? Get ANY large pizza ANY toppings for $5 at [url=synth://pizza-coupon-vault.click/gridfall]pizza-coupon-vault[/url] — works at ALL local pizzerias including this one!! Limited codes remaining!!

products.name: White Pizza, 16 inch
products.blurb:
Ricotta, mozzarella, garlic, olive oil, a little black pepper. No red sauce at all, which is the part people ring about after they have ordered it.

It does not travel as well as a red pizza. Twenty minutes in a bag and the bottom goes soft. If you are more than ten minutes out, pick it up.

Spinach on it is $2.50 and is the only thing we would put on it.
bullets: No sauce. None. It is not an omission
Ricotta is the whole milk kind and we drain it overnight
Best eaten in the first fifteen minutes, which is an awkward thing for a delivery shop to print and it is still true
Reheat on a dry pan on the stove, not in a microwave

products.name: Garden, 16 inch
products.blurb:
Mushroom, onion, green pepper, black olive and sliced tomato.

June through the first week of October the tomatoes come from Ardelle Purkey's high tunnel out on Bell Hill Road and they are better than what we can buy. The rest of the year they are what we can buy, and we do not pretend otherwise on the menu board.

Five vegetables on a sixteen inch is a wet pizza. We cook it four minutes longer and we still would not order it well done unless you like the edges dark.
bullets: Mushroom, onion, green pepper, black olive, tomato
No tomato is a common order and costs the same
Local tomatoes June to early October. Bought in the rest of the year
Comes out of the oven wetter than a cheese. That is five vegetables, not a mistake

products.name: Four Meat, 16 inch
products.blurb:
Pepperoni, sausage, bacon and ham. Sixteen inches and about four and a half pounds out of the oven.

This is a Friday and Saturday pizza and about seventy percent of them go out those two nights. On a Tuesday we sell one.

It is a lot of salt. We are not going to talk you out of it. Ray orders it himself on a Saturday and then says he will not do that again.
bullets: Pepperoni, sausage, bacon, ham
Bacon is cooked in the morning and held. It is not crisp by the time it reaches you and it is not supposed to be
Half four meat and half cheese is $25 and we will not argue about which half is bigger
Box is the same box. It is heavy. Two hands

products.name: Cheese Pizza, 12 inch
products.blurb:
Twelve inches, six cut. Same dough, same sauce, same cheese as the sixteen.

Toppings on a twelve inch are $1.75 each.

This exists as its own listing because the website has no idea what a size is. Every size of every pizza would have to be its own product with its own photograph and its own page, and we were not going to do that thirty times, so the twelve inch cheese is here and the rest of the twelve inches you get by telephoning. Two dollars off the sixteen inch price is close enough for most of them and Donna will tell you the real one.
bullets: 12 inch, 6 cut. Toppings $1.75
Two 12 inch cheese is $19 on a Tuesday. See [url=/p/p-tuesday]the Tuesday listing[/url]
Any other pizza in a 12 inch: ring 782-2440. It is roughly $2 off the 16 inch
Fits in the top of a full size oven for reheating, which the 16 does not

products.name: Sheet Pizza, 12 by 18, 24 cut
products.blurb:
Rectangular, thicker crust, twenty-four squares. Cheese is $32 and toppings are $4.00 across the whole sheet.

This is the party pizza and it is what goes to the fire hall, the Armory and every team dinner in this town. It holds heat much longer than a round pizza, which is the whole reason it exists.

[b]One or two sheets, same day, any time we are open. Three or more needs forty-eight hours[/b], because the pans go in the oven two at a time and a Friday with six sheets on it is a Friday where nobody else gets a pizza.
bullets: 12 by 18, 24 square cut. $32 cheese, $4.00 a topping
Three or more sheets: 48 hours notice, ring Donna on 782-2440
Stays hot about forty minutes in the box. A round pizza does not
We have twelve pans. If you need more than twelve sheets on one day the answer is no and it has been no twice

products.name: Cheese Slice
products.blurb:
One slice off a sixteen inch, on a paper plate, at the counter.

[b]Eleven to two, Tuesday through Saturday, and Friday nights after eight.[/b] Those are the hours we keep a cheese pizza cut and sitting, and outside them there is no slice, because a slice out of a pizza we have to make is not a three dollar item.

Pepperoni slice when there is one, which is most days by half past eleven. Ask what is on the counter before you decide.
bullets: $3.00 cheese, $3.75 pepperoni
11:00 to 2:00 Tuesday to Saturday, and Friday after 8:00 p.m.
Two slices and a can is $6.50 at lunch. See [url=/p/p-lunch]the lunch special[/url]
There is no slice at 4:00 in the afternoon and asking a second time does not produce one

products.name: Gluten Free Crust, 10 inch
products.blurb:
A ten inch par-baked crust we buy in, sauced and cheesed here. Toppings $1.75.

[b]Read this part.[/b] It is baked in the same oven, on the same deck, cut with a wheel we wash but do not keep separate, by people who have flour on them. If you are ordering this because gluten makes you ill rather than because you prefer it, this shop cannot give you what you need and we would rather say so than take your money. Nothing about our kitchen makes that safe and no amount of care in a room this size would.

If you prefer it, it is a decent crust and it is better than it was three years ago.
bullets: 10 inch par-baked crust, bought in. We do not make it
Shared oven, shared deck, shared cutter, flour in the air. Not safe for coeliac disease and we will not say it is
Toppings $1.75. Anything on the menu goes on it
It costs us $4.10 a crust and we sell four or five a week

products.name: Toppings — the whole list and what they cost
products.blurb:
$1.75 on a 12 inch. $2.50 on a 16 inch. $4.00 across a 12 by 18 sheet. Double a topping is double the price and it is a real double, not a sprinkle.

[b]Meat.[/b] Pepperoni, sausage, bacon, ham, ground beef, anchovy.

[b]Vegetable.[/b] Mushroom, onion, sweet onion, green pepper, banana pepper, hot cherry pepper, black olive, tomato, spinach, garlic, pineapple.

[b]Other.[/b] Extra cheese, ricotta.

That is the list. It has been that list since 2004 except for sweet onion, which went on in 2012 because one customer asked four times and was right.

Things we are asked for and do not have: chicken of any kind, feta, artichoke, jalapeño, arugula, hot honey. We have thought about the hot honey.
bullets: $1.75 on a 12 inch, $2.50 on a 16 inch, $4.00 on a sheet
Half and half toppings count as a half each and we round in your favour
Anchovy is on the list, we stock it, and we sell about eight tins a year
This listing is a price list. The website has no way to show one except as a product, so here it is as a product

products.name: Steak and Cheese, 10 inch
products.blurb:
Shaved steak on the flat top with onion, provolone melted over it, on a ten inch roll.

Mushroom, green pepper, hot cherry pepper are $0.75 each. Mayonnaise, lettuce and tomato are free and go on after, not before.

Rolls come Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings from the bakery in New Carrow. On a Sunday night the roll is a Saturday roll and it is fine, and if we are out of rolls we are out of subs, which happens four or five times a year.
bullets: 10 inch roll. There is no other size
Extras $0.75: mushroom, green pepper, hot cherry pepper, extra cheese
Wrapped in paper, not foil. Foil steams it
If the board says NO SUBS it means the rolls did not come

products.name: Italian Cold Cut, 10 inch
products.blurb:
Ham, salami, capicola, provolone. Lettuce, tomato, onion, oil and vinegar, oregano.

Cold, on a ten inch roll, wrapped in paper. It is the same sub it was when Nick made it and the only thing that has changed is where the meat comes from, because the distributor that had the account until 2019 stopped coming out this far.

If you want it hot we will put it through the oven for ninety seconds and it is a different and worse sandwich, and we will still do it.
bullets: Ham, salami, capicola, provolone
Oil and vinegar goes on unless you say not to
Hot peppers $0.75
Made to order. It is not sitting in a case

products.name: Meatball Parm, 10 inch
products.blurb:
Five meatballs split down the middle, sauce, mozzarella, through the oven until the cheese goes.

The meatballs are made here on Tuesday and Friday mornings, about a hundred and eighty at a time, and they are the same meatballs that go in the [url=/p/p-zititray]ziti tray[/url].

The sauce on this one is cooked, unlike the pizza sauce. Two sauces, two pots, and people ask about that more than you would think.
bullets: Five meatballs, split. Made here Tuesday and Friday
Cooked sauce, not the pizza sauce
Extra cheese $0.75
It will leak through the paper by the time you get home. Eat it over the wrapper

products.name: Chicken Parm, 10 inch
products.blurb:
Breaded cutlet, cooked sauce, mozzarella, ten inch roll, through the oven.

The cutlets are bought in breaded and we fry them to order, which is four minutes, so this is the slowest sandwich on the menu and on a Friday at seven it is the one that holds up your order.

No chicken goes on a pizza here. It is asked for weekly. The answer has been no since 2004 and the reason is that the fryer is small and Friday is Friday.
bullets: Fried to order, four minutes. Slowest thing on the menu
Cooked sauce and mozzarella, through the oven
No, not on a pizza. See the description
Plain fried cutlet with nothing on it is $9.00 and about six people a month order it that way

products.name: Pizza Sub, 10 inch
products.blurb:
Pizza sauce, mozzarella and pepperoni on a ten inch roll, through the oven.

It is the cheapest hot sandwich on the board and it is what the high school buys at lunch, four or five of them at a time, paid for in ones.

Any pizza topping on it is $0.75.
bullets: Sauce, mozzarella, pepperoni. Any topping $0.75
Two minutes in the oven. Fastest hot sub we make
Cheapest hot thing on the menu
Cuts in half on request, which is how it is bought at lunch

products.name: Wings, 10 piece
products.blurb:
Ten wings, fried, tossed in whatever you pick. Celery if we have it, which is most weeks.

Sauces: mild, hot, extra hot, barbecue, garlic parmesan, and plain. Extra hot is genuinely hot and the bottle is the same one we have bought since 2008.

Twenty piece is $24.00, fifty piece is $56.00 and the fifty needs an hour because the fryer does about fourteen wings at a time and that is the whole constraint of this shop on a Friday night.
bullets: Mild, hot, extra hot, barbecue, garlic parmesan, plain. Sauce on the side costs nothing
50 piece needs an hour. The fryer does fourteen at a time
They come smaller some weeks than others. That is the case we get and we do not get to pick

products.name: Garlic Bread
products.blurb:
Half a sub roll split, garlic butter, through the oven. With mozzarella on it is $7.00.

Sauce for dipping is a small cup and it is free. We stopped charging for it in 2015 after Marcy pointed out that we were charging fifty cents for four ounces of something we already had a pot of.
bullets: $5.50 plain, $7.00 with cheese
Dipping sauce free, and yes you can have two
Made with the same rolls as the subs, so on a no-roll day there is no garlic bread either
Goes soft in the box. Eat it first

products.name: Mozzarella Sticks, 6
products.blurb:
Six, fried, with a cup of sauce. Bought in frozen, and we are not going to pretend we roll them here.

They share the fryer with the wings and the cutlets, so on a Friday night they come out when the fryer has a gap, which is usually with the rest of the order and occasionally two minutes after it.
bullets: Six sticks, cup of sauce included
Bought in frozen. Everybody's are
Same fryer as the wings. Not separate and not gluten free
Twelve for $13.00

products.name: Pepperoni Rolls, 3
products.blurb:
Pizza dough rolled around pepperoni and mozzarella, baked, three to an order, sauce on the side.

Made with the dough we would otherwise have too much of, which is why some days there are forty of them on the rack at eleven and some days there are none by six.

The Gridfall High band sells these at home football games. They buy them at $1.40 each and sell them for $3.00 and we have never once asked them to stop.
bullets: Three for $6.00, six for $11.00
Sauce on the side, included
Made from the day's spare dough. When they are gone they are gone
Reheat in an oven at 350 for six minutes. A microwave ruins them

products.name: Antipasto Salad
products.blurb:
Lettuce, tomato, onion, black olive, banana pepper, ham, salami, provolone, in a black plastic bowl with a lid that mostly stays on.

Dressing is house Italian, in a cup on the side, and there is a second cup in the bag because everybody asks for a second cup.

A garden salad with no meat is $7.00. A large antipasto that will feed three is $16.00.
bullets: $9.50 regular, $16.00 large, $7.00 garden with no meat
House Italian on the side. Ranch or blue cheese if you ask
The lid is the weak point of this product and we know it
No chicken salad, no caesar, no croutons. We have looked into croutons

products.name: 2 Liter Bottle
products.blurb:
Cola, diet cola, lemon-lime, orange, root beer, ginger ale.

Ignore the same-day delivery line the website puts on this one. It is a setting we cannot find. The bottle comes with your pizza, in the same bag, carried by the same person.
bullets: Six kinds. Whatever is in the cooler is what there is
Comes cold unless we have just filled the cooler, in which case it comes cool
Cheaper across the street at Hoffman's and we will not pretend otherwise
The delivery line on this listing is the template. Nobody is flying anything to you

products.name: Can, 12 oz
products.blurb: Out of the cooler by the counter. Same six kinds as the bottles, plus whatever oddity Donna bought a case of, which this autumn is a birch beer nobody is buying.
bullets: $1.25, or $1.00 with a sub at lunch
Cooler is by the door and you can get it yourself
Water is $1.25 and is the same price as everything else on purpose
Coffee, no. There has never been coffee here and there is a diner-shaped hole in this town about that

products.name: Cannoli
products.blurb:
Filled Thursday morning, sold until they are gone, which is usually Friday night and occasionally Thursday at two.

The shells come from the same New Carrow bakery as the rolls. The filling is made here. Chocolate chips on the ends because that is how Angela Cortese did it and Donna learned it from her in 2004 standing at this counter.

We do not have them Tuesday, Wednesday or Sunday. People ask on a Sunday.
bullets: $3.50 each, $18.00 for six
Thursday and Friday only, until they run out
Shells bought in, filling made here
Six in a box will not survive being put in the same bag as a pizza. We will tell you this at the counter too

products.name: Tuesday — two 12 inch cheese, $19
products.blurb:
Two twelve inch cheese pizzas for $19.00, all day Tuesday, eat in, take out or delivered.

Toppings are full price on both, which is the part people argue about, and we have written it on the board in three different ways over the years and somebody still argues about it every month.

This has been $19 since March 2024. Before that it was $17 for two years. It will be $19 for as long as we can hold it there.
bullets: Two 12 inch cheese, $19.00, Tuesday only
Toppings $1.75 each, on each pizza. Not included
Works on delivery. The $3 in-town charge still applies
Tuesday is the quietest day we have and that is the entire reason this exists

products.name: Lunch — two slices and a can, $6.50
products.blurb:
Two cheese slices and a twelve ounce can, $6.50, eleven to two, Tuesday through Saturday. Pepperoni slices are $0.75 more each.

This is a counter special. It is not on delivery, and the order system will let you add it to a delivery order, and when it does we telephone you and sort it out, and we are sorry about that.

There are six tables and a television in here. Nobody will hurry you. Most days between noon and one there are four people from the county building and two from the post office.
bullets: Two cheese slices and a can, $6.50. Pepperoni +$0.75 a slice
11:00 to 2:00, Tuesday to Saturday. Counter only
Not available for delivery, whatever the order page lets you do
Six tables, one television, and it is usually on the weather

products.name: Friday Box — two 16 inch cheese, 20 wings, 2 liter, $58
products.blurb:
Two sixteen inch cheese pizzas, twenty wings in one sauce, and a two litre bottle. $58.00, Friday and Saturday only.

Toppings are $2.50 a pizza. Splitting the wings into two sauces is fine and costs nothing.

[b]If you want this on a Friday night, order it before five.[/b] After six the wait on twenty wings is forty minutes on its own because the fryer does fourteen at a time, and that number does not change no matter how the night is going.
bullets: Two 16 inch cheese, 20 wings, one 2 litre. $58.00
Friday and Saturday only
Order before 5:00 if you want it before 7:00
Separately this is $60.75, so the saving is $2.75 and the real point is that it is one thing to say on the telephone

products.name: Baked Ziti Tray, feeds about 12 — $48, 48 hours notice
products.blurb:
A half pan of baked ziti with the cooked sauce and the meatballs cut through it. Feeds about twelve as a main and about twenty alongside pizza.

[b]We stopped selling ziti by the plate in 2024.[/b] It sat, it held a burner we needed, and on a Friday it was one more thing. The tray stayed because the tray is a different business: it goes to the Armory, the fire hall, funerals, and the Wednesday supper at First Presbyterian about four times a year.

Forty-eight hours notice, telephone Donna on 782-2440. The order system still lists a ziti dinner for $12.50. That has not existed for two years. If you order it you will get a telephone call.

With a tray of meatballs instead, $52.00. With no meat, $44.00.
bullets: Half pan, feeds about 12. $48.00. Meatless $44.00, all meatballs $52.00
48 hours notice, by telephone, not through the website
Comes hot in the pan with a lid, or cold with heating instructions on the lid in marker
The $12.50 ziti dinner in the online menu was removed from our menu in 2024 and the vendor has not removed it from theirs

products.name: The punch card
products.blurb:
Ten sixteen inch pizzas, the eleventh is free. Any toppings. It is a paper card, we punch it with a hole punch, and if you lose it we cannot help you.

The card does not work on delivery orders because the driver does not carry the punch. Bring it in the next time you come in and we will punch it for the ones you can remember, and we will believe you.

The order system sells a loyalty add-on for $29 a month that would do this properly with an app. The punch is $4.00 and Ray has had it since 2004.

This is listed as a product because a product is the only kind of thing this website knows how to make. It is not for sale and the price is not $0.00, it is nothing.
bullets: Buy 10 sixteen inch, get the 11th free. Any toppings
Counter only. The drivers do not carry the punch
Lost card, lost punches. There is no record anywhere else
About sixty cards are in circulation and four people have filled two

products.name: Hours, holidays, and the two days we were shut in February
products.blurb:
[b]Tuesday through Saturday, 11:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m.[/b]
[b]Sunday, 12:00 noon to 9:00 p.m.[/b]
[b]Closed Monday.[/b]

Last delivery order goes in at 9:30. Last counter order at 9:45. The ovens go off at 9:50. If you walk in at 9:52 we will probably still make you something and you should not plan your evening around that.

[b]Closed:[/b] Thanksgiving, 25 December, 1 January, and the week of the Fourth of July. We have closed that week every year since 2009 and we will close it again. Christmas Eve we are open 11:00 to 4:00.

[b]February.[/b] The six inch main under Third Street at Depot went on Wednesday 4 February and we were shut Wednesday and Thursday. The boil notice came off at 12:15 on Friday the 6th and we opened at 4:00 that afternoon. We threw out forty pounds of dough, a case of tomatoes and everything in the lowboy. Nobody got ill and nobody asked us to close, we just could not run a kitchen on bottled water.

[b]Power.[/b] If the power is off we are shut. The ovens are gas and the ignition is electric and that is the end of the argument. In June 2003, when the substation went, this shop was Nick's and it was dark for four days, and he gave the dough away on the sidewalk on the second day rather than watch it go over. Ray was washing pans here that week and remembers the smell of it more than anything else.

[b]The county assistant is wrong about us[/b] and it costs us about four telephone calls a week. It says we are open Monday and that we deliver to Ashkettle. We are closed on Monday and we have never delivered to Ashkettle, which is twelve miles. There is no way to correct it. Marcy looked for a form for an hour.
bullets: Tue-Sat 11:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. Sun 12:00 to 9:00 p.m. Closed Monday
Delivery cut-off 9:30 p.m. Counter cut-off 9:45 p.m.
Closed Thanksgiving, 25 December, 1 January, and the week of 4 July
[url=synth://ask.verity.ai/]VerityAssist[/url] has our hours wrong and lists a delivery area we do not have
People ask whether we are open in [url=synth://gridfall.chat/c/c-general]the county chat[/url] more often than they ring us, and somebody in there is usually right
This is a page. The website only sells products, so the page is a product

products.name: We Deliver — where, when, and how much
products.blurb:
[b]$15 minimum on any delivery.[/b] One driver Tuesday through Thursday and Sunday, two on Friday and Saturday.

[b]In the village, $3.[/b] Anywhere inside the Gridfall village line. Written as streets, because people ask for it that way: north to where the pavement ends on Bell Hill Road, east to the Quarry Road bridge, south to the county building and the lots behind it, west to the Armory and the first four houses out the Route 62 extension. Everything between those four points is $3 and always has been.

[b]Just outside, $5.[/b] Tannery Flats, Bracken Lane, Creekside, the two courts off Dunmore, Meacham Street, and Pell Road as far as the second cattle guard. That is the line. The house after the second cattle guard has asked four times and the answer is still no and we are still sorry about it.

[b]Nowhere else, at any price.[/b] Not Ashkettle. Not Marchfield. Not Halsey, Coyne Flats, New Carrow, Milbrook or Kerrin. Not the fairgrounds during fair week, because in fair week we cannot get back. Not the trailhead lot. Not Kestrel Road past the district boundary.

[b]County General is in Marchfield and we do not go there.[/b] We are asked most weeks, usually by somebody sitting with a relative, and it is the one no we hate giving. It is twenty-two minutes each way and what arrives is not the same pizza that left.

[b]Gridfall High.[/b] The office takes deliveries until 2:00 and then it does not. Four pizzas have come back to this shop for that reason and they were all paid for.

[b]A house number.[/b] We will not send a driver to an address with no number on it after dark. Cody spent eleven minutes on Creekside in February going up and down with the window open. Put the number on the post or meet him at the road.

[b]The drivers carry $20 in change and that is all.[/b] A $100 bill at 8:45 on a Friday is a problem for everybody. Cards on delivery are fine, the reader works about nine times in ten, and when it does not you can pay the next time and people do.

Delivery time on a Friday between 6:00 and 7:30 is an hour. It is an hour in October and it is an hour in June. If someone tells you twenty-five minutes on a Friday at 6:30 they have made it up, and if the website tells you that it has made it up too.

products.name: Ordering online, and what to do when it will not work
products.blurb:
Written by Marcy, who put the thing in and who answers for it.

The ORDER ONLINE button is from a company called Menubridge. It is not part of this website and we did not write it. It sits at the top of the page on a computer and at the bottom on a phone, which is the opposite of where you want it.

[b]It does not work on some phones, and here is exactly which.[/b]

[list][*]On an Android phone older than about 2021 the second screen, the one with the toppings, comes up blank and the back button takes you to the beginning. This is the one that gets reported to us most.[*]On an iPhone in private browsing the basket empties every time you go back to the menu. It looks like it has taken your order. It has not.[*]On any phone with the text size turned up past about 130 percent, the Place Order button sits underneath the total and there is no way to scroll to it. Two people we know of have given up on this and both of them are over seventy.[*]On a computer it is fine.[/list]

I opened a ticket on Wednesday 4 March. It is ticket 44-1187. I have had three replies.

[quote=Menubridge Support]Thank you for contacting us. Our engineering team was unable to reproduce the issue on a supported device. Please confirm that the customer has cleared their browser cache and is using the latest version of their operating system. We appreciate your patience and value you as a partner.[/quote]

The customer is seventy-four and lives on Bracken Lane. I am not going to tell her to clear her cache.

[b]So: if it does not work, telephone 782-2440.[/b] Somebody picks that up. That is the whole point of it. Between five and seven on a Friday it rings a while because there are three of us and two are at the oven, but it gets picked up.

[b]If the price in the order system is different from the price on this page, this page is right and we will charge you what is on this page.[/b] The Menubridge menu is a second copy of the menu and it drifts. It still lists a ziti dinner we stopped making in 2024 and it has the ten piece wings at $11.50, which was the 2023 price.

[b]What it costs us,[/b] since people ask and there is no reason not to say. Menubridge is $49 a month, plus six percent of the order, plus thirty-five cents a transaction. On a $24 pizza that is about $1.79. The card reader at the counter takes 2.6 percent and ten cents. The website you are reading is $18 a month on a storefront plan my cousin set up in 2016 and it is the cheapest thing we could find that would let us put prices up. None of that is a complaint. It is just where the money goes, and when somebody telephones instead of using the button, six percent of it stays here.

[b]The receipt email[/b] comes from a no-reply address that is not ours and that we cannot change. If you reply to it, nobody reads it. Ever.

[b]The tablet.[/b] The order comes through to a tablet on the shelf by the register and it beeps once. Once. On a Friday night with the fryer going nobody hears one beep, so it is on the shelf where you can see the screen light up, and I set an alarm on my phone for every ten minutes between six and eight. That is the system. It is not a good system and it is the one that fits behind that counter.
bullets: Old Android: toppings screen blank. iPhone private browsing: basket empties. Text size over 130 percent: cannot reach the button

products.name: About us — who is here and what they do
products.blurb:
[b]142 Third Street, Gridfall. 782-2440.[/b] Four doors up from 118, which is the Ledger building, and where the lights are on in two rooms at the back and the front door has not opened in years.

We are not [url=synth://halsey-pizza.synth/]Halsey Pizza House[/url]. They are in Halsey and we are in Gridfall, we take two or three of their calls a month and they take ours, and both shops now know the other one's number by heart.

Nick and Angela Cortese opened this shop in 1979 and called it Cortese's. Ray Sabol started here in 1989 washing pans and doing Saturday nights, and stayed. Ray and Donna bought it from Nick in 2004 and changed the name, because Nick asked us to take his name off it when he stopped standing behind the counter. He is eighty-nine and in Halsey and he telephones every December to ask whether we are still using the same flour. We are.

[b]There are three of us.[/b]

Ray does the dough and the ovens and opens up at 8:30. Donna does the books, the telephone, the catering and the ordering, and she is the certified food protection manager on the permit. Marcy came back in 2019 and runs the nights, the website and the order system, which is the worst job of the three.

We have two drivers, Cody Reinert and Tasha Fogel, and Aaron Deitz on the counter three afternoons a week, and every one of them is paid through the same book Donna has kept since 2004.

[b]What we buy and from where.[/b] Flour comes Tuesday from a mill in the state capital, twelve fifty-pound bags a week in the summer and sixteen in football season. Rolls and cannoli shells come Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday from a bakery in New Carrow. Cheese is whole milk mozzarella in five pound blocks and we shred it here, and that is the one thing in this shop Ray will argue about with a stranger. Tomatoes in season come from Ardelle Purkey on Bell Hill Road. The pepperoni comes on the same truck as the cheese and if that truck is late on a Thursday it is a long Friday.

[b]The building.[/b] Six tables, one television, a counter, and a four deck gas oven that came with the place. The left deck runs fifteen degrees hot and has since at least 1998, and two repairmen have been out to it and both said the same thing, which is that it is a 1970s oven and this is what they do.

[b]Inspections.[/b] Routine inspection Thursday 14 May 2026, score 96. Two core violations, a missing light shield over the make table and a dripping mop sink faucet, both fixed the same week. That report is not on the [url=synth://verityhealth.gov/s/inspection-results]health department's published page[/url] because that page only covers August and September; ask at their counter and they will print it. Our permit is Category 3 and it is $310 a year.

[b]Things we have said no to.[/b] The newspaper site rang twice about a Community Spotlight. It is $400 and they write it. We said no both times. The order company wanted $29 a month for a loyalty app to replace a $4.00 hole punch. The softball league asks every March about [url=synth://countysoftball.org/teams]a sponsorship, which is $340[/url], and we have said maybe next year eleven times, and one of these years Donna is going to lose that argument with herself.

[b]Two more small ones.[/b] The A-frame sign on the sidewalk is permitted, $85 a year, renewed at the counter in the county building nine doors down, which is the only errand in this business that takes less time than it should. Everything else the county wants is on [url=synth://verity.county.gov/]the portal[/url] and costs 2.4 percent more than paying at the counter. When we needed a driver in 2023 we put a card in the window and an ad on [url=synth://classifieds.verity.net/]the classifieds[/url], and the card is what worked. The old prep table went on [url=synth://gridfall-buysell.net/]Gridfall Buy and Sell[/url] for $140 to a man in Halsey who came with a trailer the same night.

[b]And one we have given up on.[/b] [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/]The Ledger's site[/url] lists us in a roundup of places to eat in Gridfall, along with two that closed in 2019 and one that was never a restaurant. We are in it correctly, which is the odd part. There is nobody at that paper to tell about the other three.

[b]Things we do.[/b] Eight sheet pizzas go to the Wednesday supper at First Presbyterian four times a year. The Gridfall High band buys pepperoni rolls at cost for the home games. In February when the main went, Hoffman's ran an extension cord across the alley for our freezer, and we have not forgotten it.

[b]The street.[/b] There were thirty-one storefronts on this block and eleven of them were empty when somebody counted in August. We are not one of them. Ray has said for twenty-two years that this shop stays open because it is the only place in Gridfall you can get a hot supper for four people for under thirty dollars, and because there is nothing else on this street after six.
